title: Machine learning insights into obesity related genes XRCC4 and ARL6 in obstructive sleep apnea.
authors: Chen, Yong-Chao; Wang, Xin; Yuan, Hu-Wei; Pan, Yan-Wen; Pan, Hong-Guang; Teng, Yi-Shu
one_liner_zh: 该研究用机器学习分析OSA肥胖相关基因表达，筛选XRCC4和ARL6作为生物标志物，但仅涉及基因表达统计，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: PURPOSE: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is highly prevalent among obese individuals, with a complex and bidirectional relationship wherein obesity not only serves as a primary risk factor for OSA but also exacerbates its severity. This interconnection may be influenced by a set of shared genes; however, the molecular mechanisms linking obesity and OSA remain poorly characterized. This study aims to explore the molecular signatures and mechanisms underlying obesity-related genes in OSA. METHODS: We analyzed gene expression data from the GSE135917 dataset (training dataset) to identify obesity-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in OSA patients. Functional enrichment analyses and machine learning approaches were employed to explore associated biological pathways and develop predictive models. The findings were subsequently validated in an independent dataset, GSE38792. RESULTS: A total of 25 significant DEGs were identified, with 13 genes upregulated and 12 downregulated in OSA patients. Functional enrichment analysis revealed associations with insulin resistance, lipid metabolism, and Toll-like receptor signaling. Machine learning models highlighted XRCC4 and ARL6 as potential diagnostic biomarkers, validated in the independent GSE38792 dataset. XRCC4's role in DNA repair may be compromised by obesity-related inflammation and oxidative stress, while ARL6 is implicated in adipocyte function and intracellular signaling. CONCLUSION: Our findings contribute to the understanding of obesity-related genes in OSA, proposing XRCC4 and ARL6 as novel biomarkers. This study underscores the complexity of the interactions between obesity and OSA, paving the way for future research into their shared molecular pathways.
abstract_zh: 目的：阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停（OSA）在肥胖个体中高度流行，二者之间存在复杂且双向的关系，其中肥胖不仅是OSA的主要风险因素，还会加剧其严重程度。这种相互关联可能受一组共享基因的影响；然而，连接肥胖与OSA的分子机制仍未被充分阐明。本研究旨在探索OSA中肥胖相关基因的分子特征及机制。方法：我们分析了GSE135917数据集（训练数据集）中的基因表达数据，以识别OSA患者中肥胖相关的差异表达基因（DEGs）。采用功能富集分析和机器学习方法探索相关生物学通路并开发预测模型。研究结果随后在独立数据集GSE38792中进行了验证。结果：共识别出25个显著的DEGs，其中OSA患者中有13个基因上调，12个基因下调。功能富集分析揭示了与胰岛素抵抗、脂质代谢和Toll样受体信号传导的关联。机器学习模型突出显示了XRCC4和ARL6作为潜在的诊断生物标志物，并在独立数据集GSE38792中得到了验证。XRCC4在DNA修复中的作用可能因肥胖相关炎症和氧化应激而受损，而ARL6则涉及脂肪细胞功能和细胞内信号传导。结论：我们的发现有助于理解OSA中肥胖相关基因，提出XRCC4和ARL6作为新型生物标志物。本研究强调了肥胖与OSA之间相互作用的复杂性，为未来研究其共享分子通路铺平了道路。
